_comment: Single source of truth for TinyZKP pricing + plan limits. Read by parity tests in both crates/hc-server/src/usage_log.rs and billing/tests/test_pricing_parity.py — drift between either Rust or Python and this file fails CI. Edit this file FIRST when changing pricing; the parity tests will fail loudly until both sides catch up.
_plan_visibility: Stripe self-serve checkout exposes 'free', 'developer', and 'scale' (plus a usage-based Compute product handled outside this rate sheet). The 'team' plan is retained here as a sales-only/grandfathered contract — provisioned by hand via billing/provision_tenant.py with plan=team — because the rate sheet supports it but there is no Stripe self-serve path. Marketing surfaces (site/index.html, site/signup.html) must NOT advertise Team as a checkout option; site/docs.html documents it for completeness.

billing_meters._comment: Declares which Stripe meter each plan bills through. sync_usage.py and parity tests enforce this mapping. 'compute' tenants are metered by raw trace steps via trace_step_usage ($0.50/1M steps); all other plans use proof_usage (discounted cents-per-proof). The monthly_cap_cents on the compute plan is a coarse safety bound only — real billing is the step meter.

compute._comment: Billed via trace_step_usage meter ($0.50/1M steps), NOT the cents-per-proof tiers. monthly_cap_cents is a coarse safety bound only.

plan_aliases._comment: Legacy plan slugs from prior pricing iterations. 'standard' was an early developer-tier label. 'pro' was the Stripe product label that succeeded 'scale'; Cloudflare checkout maps scale -> pro at the Stripe layer, but tenants whose DB row stored plan='pro' should resolve to the scale rate sheet.
